note: Community weight is high on both sides of the divide, so this part of the global literature does transfer.
Material conditions dominate everywhere, and in the Indonesian evidence they are better supported than masculinity as a barrier.
The one masculinity norm that is near-identical across the divide. The demand to be tough and the fear of appearing weak travel.
The single largest divergence in the corpus, and it runs both ways: takdir framing delays care, while ngelakoni makes adherence a religious duty.
Read individually, a man who leaves his health to his wife looks like avoidance. Read relationally, the same arrangement is a household securing care through its ordinary division of labour.
Codified rather than merely cultural: Marriage Law No. 1/1974, Islamic nafaqah, and adat requiring public financial demonstration.
Gotong royong obliges assistance and rukun subordinates the individual to the collective. The same reach carries care and judgement.
Jamu, prayer and traditional healers sit alongside Puskesmas, and the formal system is often the last resort rather than the first.
Indonesian peer research separates teman nongkrong from teman curhat and finds company abundant while confiding is rare. Adding more men to the room does not produce disclosure.

Masculinity ideology explained 11.4% of variance in help-seeking attitudes among 115 young men, but showed no significant correlation with primary-care use among 134 Surabaya men. Not established as the main Indonesian barrier.

note: Zero randomised wording experiments on Indonesian men exist in the entire corpus. Every wording recommendation on this site is a hypothesis.
